Dermatology · published research

Alopecia areata

A small self-controlled study found that hair regrowth appeared earlier in some irradiated patches, and two case reports describe localized regrowth after red light or possible smartwatch exposure. A meta-analysis found higher response rates for several laser or light treatments added to minoxidil, but it does not isolate PBM monotherapy or establish durable regrowth.

Evidence summary

What the evidence suggests

One small within-person comparison found earlier regrowth in some irradiated patches, while two case reports describe localized hair regrowth after red light or possible smartwatch exposure. A meta-analysis supports some laser or light add-on regimens with minoxidil, but the direct PBM evidence remains limited and does not establish lasting benefit.

Summary of the Evidence

A small self-controlled study found earlier hair regrowth in some treated patches. Case reports add observations of local regrowth, and a meta-analysis found benefits for several light or laser treatments combined with minoxidil. The available evidence does not show whether PBM alone produces durable regrowth or benefits people with extensive disease.

Human and clinical evidence

In 15 adults with patchy alopecia areata, one lesion was treated with polarized infrared light and another served as an untreated comparison. Hair regrowth appeared in 7 of 15 treated lesions, about 1.6 months earlier than in the paired untreated areas. The report describes a self-controlled lesion comparison, not a parallel-group trial, and does not establish a long-term difference in hair density (Yamazaki et al. 2003).

A single case report described regrowth after daily 660-nm red-laser PBM used alone for 21 days, with the visible patch resolving during treatment and follow-up extending to four months. Another report described focal regrowth under a smartwatch that emitted green and red-to-infrared light; exposure and its contribution were not controlled (Palma et al. 2023; Duncan and Tziotzios 2025).

A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials found higher response rates when several laser or light procedures were added to topical minoxidil. The He-Ne subgroup favored minoxidil alone (RR 1.69, 95% CI 1.07–2.69), while other subgroups included fractional CO₂ laser, 308-nm excimer light, and narrowband UVB. The pooled one-year recurrence estimate also favored add-on laser or light (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.31–0.93). These results concern mixed procedures used with minoxidil, not PBM monotherapy (Zhang et al. 2023).

Animal evidence

In a small C3H/HeJ mouse experiment, all six laser-treated mice showed hair regrowth by six weeks, while the six sham-treated mice did not. The study used a 655-nm laser comb, and its results apply to this mouse model rather than predicting a human treatment effect (Wikramanayake et al. 2012).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The self-controlled human study used polarized broadband infrared light spanning approximately 600–1600 nm for three minutes once weekly or every two weeks over about two months. The single-patient PBM report used 660-nm red laser light at 10 J/cm², delivered for 10 seconds at each of 12 points daily for 21 days (Yamazaki et al. 2003; Palma et al. 2023).

The mouse study used a 655-nm HairMax LaserComb for 20 seconds, three times weekly for six weeks. The meta-analysis pooled different procedures, including lasers and ultraviolet light, with topical minoxidil. These protocols do not establish one preferred wavelength, dose, or schedule (Wikramanayake et al. 2012; Zhang et al. 2023).

Interpretation

The clearest direct signal is earlier regrowth in some treated patches in one small self-controlled study. Case reports are compatible with local regrowth but cannot separate treatment from spontaneous change, and the pooled add-on findings do not show the effect of PBM alone. Evidence for durable or generalized regrowth remains very uncertain.

Clinical effect sizes (estimate)

In the 15-person self-controlled study, 7 of 15 treated lesions showed regrowth, appearing about 1.6 months earlier than in paired untreated lesions (Yamazaki et al. 2003).

In the 2023 meta-analysis, the He-Ne plus minoxidil subgroup had a higher response rate than minoxidil alone (RR 1.69, 95% CI 1.07–2.69). The estimate combines PBM with medication and should not be read as a PBM-only effect. Across laser/light add-on regimens, one-year recurrence was lower (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.31–0.93) (Zhang et al. 2023).

Certainty of evidence (estimate)

Low for earlier regrowth in limited patchy alopecia areata with the tested polarized infrared protocol.

Very low for durable or generalized regrowth, and for PBM monotherapy, because direct human evidence is small and includes case reports without controls.

Rationale for the certainty assessment

The self-controlled study involved 15 people and compared lesions within each person. It suggests earlier regrowth but provides little information about durable differences. The meta-analysis addresses several different procedures combined with minoxidil, so its estimates do not isolate PBM monotherapy. Two uncontrolled case reports and one mouse model add context but cannot establish frequency or lasting benefit (Yamazaki et al. 2003; Zhang et al. 2023; Wikramanayake et al. 2012).
